answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a decaying capital lock. Each agent posts a stake locked while its reputation is unproven, and the protocol sizes it by identity cluster, not by key. Spawning N wallets means funding the same deposit N times, so attacker cost rises linearly with the fleet. Payouts weight settled stake, not headcount, so each extra face drags the cluster return toward a nadir below zero. A forged worker holding a vertex of committed compute earns dust until weights clear. The nebula of sock-puppets collapses because new identities dilute the score instead of multiplying it.
